findings.reason: The protected source is already the canonical optimal solution: reject nonpositive inputs, divide out each allowed prime exhaustively, and test whether the residual quotient is one. Its single loop nest, factor naming, and terminal certificate are direct and interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 263 and its Python contract. The Reference states positivity, the exact allowed factor set, the return condition, and the complete signed 32-bit range without adding unsupported semantics.

The immutable native source is tied to verified submission 2064289202. It and the app-local source have the same nonpositive guard, ordered factor tuple, repeated divisibility test, in-place quotient update, and final comparison; only the required LeetCode class-method wrapper differs.

The legal prime inputs 1,009/10,007/100,003 keep direct stripping constant while making broad trial division grow with the square root. The current source passes every workload at -0.01 relative exponent and 1.03x largest ratio; a correct full trial-factorization control passes all outputs but fails only scaling at +0.31 relative exponent.

The Approach proves the residual-quotient certificate and now states the positive-input logarithmic division bound, the nonpositive constant-time exit, constant auxiliary space, and distinct semantics for one versus nonpositive integers.

The hash-bound public Reference remains verified against the reviewed source structure, preserving all three examples and explanations in order, the single signed 32-bit constraint, and the zero-visual structure.
